Thanks Sam — quick reply while I sync internally.

Short answer: we can do this without forcing 2am calls. Because US DST starts on Sun Mar 14 (US), and EU DST follows on Sun Mar 28, the week of Mar 15 is okay for a larger overlap — but it shifts relative offsets for East/West US vs CET. To avoid confusion, here are two practical options that keep everyone in reasonable hours:

Option A — US-friendly mid-morning / EU late-afternoon
- Tue Mar 16, 10:30 PT / 13:30 ET / 18:30 CET — decent for EU (end of day), OK for US east (early afternoon).

Option B — EU-friendly late morning / US early afternoon
- Wed Mar 17, 11:00 CET / 10:00 GMT? (pre-DST) / 05:00 PT (oops — that pushes West) — actually not great.

Let me reframe with accurate offsets for clarity (apologies for the confusion): because US will have already sprung forward, Pacific is UTC-7 and Central Europe (CET) is still UTC+1, so the gap is 8 hours. That means a 16:00 CET slot is 08:00 PT, which is an acceptable start for many US West engineers.

Option C — balanced overlap (my recommended)
- Tue Mar 16, 16:00 CET / 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET — 45 minutes, with recording for APAC colleagues that join later.

Can you confirm which of these works for your core attendees? I'm attaching a short agenda and a tz-converter .ics I can push once we pick a slot. If you want, Marissa will join the call for a product deep-dive and Vivek can outline dedicated capacity/SLAs if procurement flags come up.

Best,
Priyom Das
